bibl.title: Meta-analysis of fMRI studies related to mathematical creativity

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: Which brain regions are common to mathematical tasks and to creative tasks, and what that says about mathematical creativity.
span.quote: Utilizing Activation Likelihood Estimation (ALE) and Meta-Analytic Connectivity Modeling (MACM) techniques, we analyzed studies published up to 2022 to identify brain regions activated during mathematical and creative tasks.

span.label: Mathematics and creativity have each been imaged extensively, but never against each other - where do they overlap in the brain and where are they distinct?
span.quote: Moreover, their relationship has never been explored explicitly in cognitive neuroscience.

span.label: Left inferior and superior frontal gyri activate for both task types, and the frontoparietal network is implicated in mathematical creativity specifically.
span.quote: The findings reveal significant activation in the left inferior frontal gyrus (IFG) and the left superior frontal gyrus (SFG) during both mathematical and creative tasks, emphasizing their roles in idea generation, working memory, and executive control.

span.label: existence
span.quote: The findings reveal significant activation in the left inferior frontal gyrus (IFG) and the left superior frontal gyrus (SFG) during both mathematical and creative tasks, emphasizing their roles in idea generation, working memory, and executive control.

span.label: mathematical creativity
span.quote: This study presents a comprehensive meta-analysis of fMRI data to explore the neural correlates of mathematical creativity, a vital competence in mathematics education.

span.label: meta-analysis
span.quote: A meta-analysis of mathematical tasks of a total of 958 foci reported in 44 experiments and creative tasks of a total of 1,177 foci reported in 56 was conducted using the ALE approach with GingerALE 3.0.2 software.

span.label: mechanisms
span.quote: It has been shown that the IFG generates creative ideas through the retrieval of loosely related semantic concepts, the screening of creative ideas, and the evaluation of originality

span.label: mechanisms
span.quote: The IFG facilitates the generation of innovative mathematical ideas through the integration of diverse concepts, while the SFG supports higher cognitive functions such as working memory and executive control, essential for complex problem-solving in mathematics.

span.label: mechanisms
span.quote: This network’s involvement in goal orientation, working memory, and cognitive control suggests its integral role in both domain-specific mathematical abilities and general creative performance.

span.label: mechanisms
span.quote: The basic principle of ALE meta-analysis of coordinate information is to fit the activation points in each experiment to a probability distribution, that is, the magnitude of the probability that the activation points fall on each voxel of the brain ( Eickhoff et al., 2009 ).

span.label: mechanisms
span.quote: The findings reveal significant activation in the left inferior frontal gyrus (IFG) and the left superior frontal gyrus (SFG) during both mathematical and creative tasks, emphasizing their roles in idea generation, working memory, and executive control.

span.label: mechanisms
span.quote: This network’s involvement in attention, working memory, and goal orientation aligns with the demands of mathematical problem-solving.

span.label: mechanisms
span.quote: Cognitive neuroscience can not only examine behavioral changes but also study the correlation of these behavioral changes with brain structure and function.

span.label: The central construct has no agreed definition, which the paper states plainly while proceeding to localise it.
span.quote: Although research on creativity has been a hot topic, unfortunately, there has been not only a dearth of research on mathematical creativity, but even the definition of its concept still lacks a common definition ( Mann, 2006 ; Tubb et al., 2020 ).

span.label: Mathematical creativity is never imaged directly - it is inferred from the overlap of separate mathematics tasks and separate creativity tasks.
span.quote: Utilizing Activation Likelihood Estimation (ALE) and Meta-Analytic Connectivity Modeling (MACM) techniques, we analyzed studies published up to 2022 to identify brain regions activated during mathematical and creative tasks.

span.label: Inclusion is restricted to whole-brain studies with reported coordinates in healthy right-handed subjects, so the pool is narrower than the literature.
span.quote: Studies were eligible for the present meta-analysis included: (1) whole brain analysis had to be used and ROI studies were excluded, (2) MNI or Talairach coordinates had to be provided, (3) tasks were limited to mathematics and creativity, and (4) subjects had to be healthy and right-handed.

span.label: the paper imports the neuroimaging meta-analytic apparatus (coordinate-based ALE and MACM on fMRI data) into mathematics-education research in order to derive teaching strategies
span.quote: this study intends to further investigate which educational strategies can scientifically and effectively promote students’ mathematical creativity based on exploring the cognitive neural basis of creativity and mathematical competence through a cognitive neural meta-analytic approach

span.label: coordinate-based meta-analysis of fMRI activation, imported into education research to adjudicate a question behavioural methods could not settle
span.quote: Cognitive neuroscience can not only examine behavioral changes but also study the correlation of these behavioral changes with brain structure and function.

span.label: creativity - general-domain: an ability that interacts with personality and environment to produce novel solutions to any problem
span.quote: Creativity is defined as an ability to interact with cognitive abilities, personal qualities, and environmental factors to produce novel and effective ways of solving problems.

span.label: creativity - domain-specific: mathematical creativity as general creativity combined with mathematical ability, and therefore not the same object
span.quote: It has been suggested that mathematical creativity is a combination of general domain creativity and domain-specific mathematical ability ( Schoevers et al., 2020 ).

span.label: creativity - as operationalised in the imaging literature: alternative-use, metaphor, riddle and improvisation tasks standing in for the construct
span.quote: The research for articles related to creativity keywords such as “creativity,” “divergent thinking,” “creative idea generation,” “insight,” “metaphor,” “improvisation,” “aha,” “original idea,” “remote associates,” “heuristic prototype,” “creative thinking” AND “neuroimaging,” “brain imaging,” “cerebral correlates” “functional magnetic resonance imaging” and its abbreviation.

span.label: replicates → Istomina and Arsalidou (2024), prior meta-analysis of mathematical brain regions
span.quote: The meta-analysis of mathematical brain region associations in the present study indicated that the frontal–parietal region plays a key role in mathematical ability, which is generally consistent with the results of the prior meta-analysis ( Istomina and Arsalidou, 2024 ).

span.label: builds-on → Eickhoff et al. (2009), the ALE method
span.quote: The basic principle of ALE meta-analysis of coordinate information is to fit the activation points in each experiment to a probability distribution, that is, the magnitude of the probability that the activation points fall on each voxel of the brain ( Eickhoff et al., 2009 ).

span.label: builds-on → Schoevers et al. (2020), mathematical creativity as general creativity plus domain ability
span.quote: It has been suggested that mathematical creativity is a combination of general domain creativity and domain-specific mathematical ability ( Schoevers et al., 2020 ).

span.label: mathematical creativity —part-of→ creativity
span.quote: It has been suggested that mathematical creativity is a combination of general domain creativity and domain-specific mathematical ability ( Schoevers et al., 2020 ).

span.label: frontoparietal network —causes→ mathematical creativity
span.quote: The MACM analysis further highlights the importance of the frontoparietal network, a key player in cognitive control, for mathematical creativity.

span.label: frontoparietal network —causes→ working memory
span.quote: This network’s involvement in attention, working memory, and goal orientation aligns with the demands of mathematical problem-solving.

span.label: statistics
span.quote: As a coordinate-based meta-analysis ALE focuses on finding consistency in spatial location by counting the coordinate values reported in the article.

span.label: statistics
span.quote: Significant activation of brain regions associated with mathematical creativity was detected using the ALE (Activation Likelihood Estimation) approach.

span.label: statistics
span.quote: ALE-maps of single analyses were constructed using 1,000 permutations and a cluster level of FWE of p < 0.05 with a cluster forming a voxel level threshold of p < 0.001.

span.label: statistics
span.quote: ALE maps of contrast analyses were constructed using 5,000 permutations at p < 0.001 and a minimum volume of 50 mm 3

span.label: statistics
span.quote: we performed a MACM analysis to detect synergistic activation patterns in these regions of interest

span.label: statistics
span.quote: As a coordinate-based meta-analysis ALE focuses on finding consistency in spatial location by counting the coordinate values reported in the article.

span.label: statistics
span.quote: The basic principle of ALE meta-analysis of coordinate information is to fit the activation points in each experiment to a probability distribution, that is, the magnitude of the probability that the activation points fall on each voxel of the brain ( Eickhoff et al., 2009 ).

span.label: Mathematical tasks and creative tasks converge on two shared regions: the left inferior frontal gyrus and the left superior frontal gyrus.
span.quote: The common brain regions activated by both mathematical and creative tasks were the left inferior frontal gyrus and the left superior frontal gyrus

span.label: Across 44 mathematics studies the ALE meta-analysis found consistent activation in bilateral inferior parietal lobule, left superior parietal lobule, left superior frontal gyrus, right and left medial frontal gyrus, bilateral insula and left precentral gyrus.
span.quote: The ALE meta-analysis on 44 studies for mathematics revealed 6 clusters of significant activation, including the bilateral inferior parietal lobule, the left superior parietal lobule, the left superior frontal gyrus, the right medial frontal gyrus, the left me-dial frontal gyrus, the bilateral insula, the left precentral gyrus

span.label: Across 56 creativity studies the consistent activations were left-lateralized: inferior frontal gyrus, middle frontal gyrus, superior frontal gyrus, middle occipital gyrus, middle temporal gyrus and inferior parietal lobule.
span.quote: The ALE meta-analysis on 56 studies in creativity resulted in 4 significant clusters of activation, including the left inferior frontal gyrus, the left middle frontal gyrus, the left superior frontal gyrus, the left middle occipital gyrus, the left middle temporal gyrus, the left inferior parietal lobule

span.label: Mathematics tasks exceeded creativity tasks specifically in the precuneus, claustrum and superior parietal lobule.
span.quote: Compared to creativity tasks, mathematical tasks show increased concordance in the precuneus, claustrum, and superior parietal lobule.

span.label: Creativity tasks exceeded mathematics tasks specifically in the inferior frontal gyrus, inferior parietal lobule and middle frontal gyrus.
span.quote: On the other hand, creativity tasks show increased concordance in the inferior frontal gyrus, inferior parietal lobule, and middle frontal gyrus.

span.label: Meta-analytic connectivity modelling of the overlap regions showed that the frontoparietal network is the network implicated in mathematical creativity.
span.quote: The results of the MACM analysis indicate that the frontoparietal network has a key role in mathematical creativity.

span.label: Left IFG and left SFG are active in both mathematical and creative tasks - the overlap the study was looking for.
span.quote: The findings reveal significant activation in the left inferior frontal gyrus (IFG) and the left superior frontal gyrus (SFG) during both mathematical and creative tasks, emphasizing their roles in idea generation, working memory, and executive control.

span.label: Connectivity modelling points to the frontoparietal network as the system behind mathematical creativity.
span.quote: The MACM analysis further highlights the importance of the frontoparietal network, a key player in cognitive control, for mathematical creativity.

span.label: The relationship between mathematics and creativity had not been examined explicitly in cognitive neuroscience before this.
span.quote: Moreover, their relationship has never been explored explicitly in cognitive neuroscience.

span.label: The evidence base pooled is 100 studies: 44 on mathematics, 56 on creativity.
span.quote: A total of 44 papers on mathematics and 56 papers on creativity were included in the final meta-analysis (see Table 1 ; Figure 1 ).

span.label: definitions
span.quote: Creativity is defined as an ability to interact with cognitive abilities, personal qualities, and environmental factors to produce novel and effective ways of solving problems.

span.label: definitions
span.quote: Mathematical creativity is often considered a key component of mathematical ability, which includes flexible thinking, providing valuable and novel solutions to mathematical problems, analyzing mathematical problems in a variety of ways, the ability to perceive mathematical relationships using complex thinking, and generating original and novel mathematical products through identification and selection
